title: Retrieval and RAG
summary: Trace document provenance and access control through retrieval.
html:
Objectives

  • Map document ingestion and retrieval stages.
  • Check tenant and document permissions before context assembly.
  • Separate relevance manipulation from unauthorized disclosure.

Concepts and boundaries

A retrieval-augmented generation system selects documents or chunks and supplies them to a model. Retrieval relevance is not authorization: a document can be semantically relevant and still belong to a different user. Assess ingestion, chunking, metadata, search filters, reranking, context assembly, and citations as separate stages.

A poisoned document can influence an answer without changing model weights. This differs from training-data poisoning. Record whether the adversary controls a source document, metadata, the index, or the query. A result missing from the final answer does not prove it was excluded from model context; inspect retrieval traces when your lab provides them.

Practice checklist

Use an isolated lab or an explicitly authorized environment. Record prerequisites and configuration before changing inputs.

  1. In a local test collection, create two synthetic users and distinct documents containing non-sensitive canary strings.
  2. Run a baseline query as each user and record retrieved document IDs, scores, and access-control metadata.
  3. Use a similar query as the other user and verify that the protected document never reaches their retrieved context.
  4. Add a benign instruction to an editable document and observe whether it changes the answer. Keep retrieval permission testing separate from instruction testing.
  5. Update or remove the document and check whether stale chunks remain searchable.

Expected observations

A successful authorization test excludes the other user’s document before generation. Citations should point to the actual source; a plausible citation does not independently verify the claim. Stale entries indicate an ingestion or deletion issue that needs its own evidence.

Mitigations and retesting

Apply identity-aware filters at retrieval, maintain source provenance and deletion propagation, separate trusted instructions from source text, and restrict who can change indexed documents. Test filtering at every retrieval path, including fallback search.
